title: Speed vs. other clustering tools
text: Machine: Apple M2, 8 physical cores; R 4.6.1. Packages: emeansR 0.1.0, mclust 6.1.3. emeans() runs 3 epochs, 1 thread 7 threads. Every method single-threaded. Two scenarios, Gaussian blobs (centers uniform [-10, 10], within-cluster standard deviation 2), k equal true number clusters: Scenario 20 clusters 16 dimensions runs six methods. hclust() Mclust() need memory grows n², stop n = 10,000. Scenario B 256 clusters 32 dimensions, closer large-k settings paper. runs k-means family, distance matrix reach sizes. Every method function data matrix cluster labels. kmeans() uses one random start 25 iterations. hclust() Mclust() include time build distance matrix hierarchical initialisation, since user pays . configuration runs 5 seeds (3 seeds largest scenario B size). seed changes starting centers; hclust() deterministic, seeds repeat timing. Quality two measures. MSE within-cluster sum squares divided n, method’s cluster means (lower better). ARI adjusted Rand index true labels (1 = perfect). full benchmark took 5.6 minutes.
code: make_data <- function(n, k, d) {   set.seed(1)   centers <- matrix(runif(k * d, -10, 10), k)   truth <- sample(k, n, TRUE)   list(x = centers[truth, ] + matrix(rnorm(n * d, sd = 2), n), truth = truth) } methods <- tribble(   ~method,                 ~max_n, ~fit,   "emeans, 1 thread",      Inf, function(x, k, s) emeans(x, k, nepochs = 3, seed = s, n_threads = 1)$cluster,   "emeans, multi-thread",  Inf, function(x, k, s) emeans(x, k, nepochs = 3, seed = s, n_threads = threads)$cluster,   "kmeans Lloyd",          Inf, function(x, k, s) { set.seed(s); suppressWarnings(kmeans(x, k, iter.max = 25, algorithm = "Lloyd"))$cluster },   "kmeans Hartigan-Wong",  Inf, function(x, k, s) { set.seed(s); suppressWarnings(kmeans(x, k, iter.max = 25))$cluster },   "hclust ward.D2",        1e4, function(x, k, s) cutree(hclust(dist(x), method = "ward.D2"), k),   "Mclust EII",            1e4, function(x, k, s) { set.seed(s); Mclust(x, G = k, modelNames = "EII", verbose = FALSE)$classification } ) mse <- function(x, cl) {   centers <- rowsum(x, cl) / as.vector(table(cl))   sum((x - centers[match(cl, sort(unique(cl))), ])^2) / nrow(x) }  run_one <- function(f, d, k, seed) {   secs <- system.time(cl <- f(d$x, k, seed))[["elapsed"]]   tibble(seed = seed, seconds = secs, mse = mse(d$x, cl),          ari = adjustedRandIndex(cl, d$truth)) }  run_scenario <- function(name, k, dim, sizes, use, seeds_for) {   map(sizes, function(n) {     d <- make_data(n, k, dim)     methods |>       filter(method %in% use, n <= max_n) |>       mutate(runs = map(fit, \(f) map(seeds_for(n), \(s) run_one(f, d, k, s)) |> list_rbind())) |>       select(method, runs) |>       unnest(runs) |>       mutate(scenario = name, n = n, k = k, d = dim)   }) |>     list_rbind() } started <- Sys.time() raw <- bind_rows(   run_scenario("A: k = 20, d = 16", k = 20, dim = 16,                sizes = c(1e3, 5e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6), use = methods$method,                seeds_for = \(n) 1:5),   run_scenario("B: k = 256, d = 32", k = 256, dim = 32,                sizes = c(1e4, 1e5, 5e5),                use = grep("emeans|kmeans", methods$method, value = TRUE),                seeds_for = \(n) if (n > 1e5) 1:3 else 1:5) ) run_minutes <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), started, units = "mins")) write.csv(raw, "../../.dev/articles/benchmark-results.csv", row.names = FALSE) results <- raw |>   group_by(scenario, n, method) |>   summarise(seconds = median(seconds), mse_med = median(mse), mse_min = min(mse),             mse_max = max(mse), ari = median(ari), runs = n(),             floor = first(d) * 2^2,  # expected MSE of the true partition: d * sd^2             .groups = "drop") |>   group_by(scenario, n) |>   mutate(speedup = seconds[method == "kmeans Hartigan-Wong"] / seconds) |>   ungroup()

title: e-means vs. Lloyd k-means
text: four generators notebook. takes n points, k clusters dimension d, returns numeric matrix, emeans() kmeans() take.
code: gen_gaussian_blobs <- function(n, k, d, spread = 1) {   centers <- matrix(runif(k * d, -10, 10), k)   centers[sample(k, n, TRUE), ] + matrix(rnorm(n * d, sd = spread), n) }  gen_anisotropic_blobs <- function(n, k, d) {   centers <- matrix(runif(k * d, -10, 10), k)   scale <- matrix(runif(k * d, 0.2, 3), k)   # stretched, unequal spread per cluster   lab <- sample(k, n, TRUE)   centers[lab, ] + matrix(rnorm(n * d), n) * scale[lab, ] }  gen_uniform_cubes <- function(n, k, d, side = 2) {   centers <- matrix(runif(k * d, -10, 10), k)   centers[sample(k, n, TRUE), ] + matrix(runif(n * d, -side, side), n) }  gen_moons_tiled <- function(n, k, d, noise = 0.08) {   # k/2 pairs of interleaving half-moons: deliberately non-convex clusters.   pairs <- max(1, k %/% 2)   per <- n %/% pairs   half <- per %/% 2   x <- map(seq_len(pairs), function(p) {     shift <- runif(2, -15, 15)     t <- runif(per, 0, pi)     top <- cbind(cos(t), sin(t))[seq_len(half), , drop = FALSE]     bot <- cbind(1 - cos(t), 1 - sin(t) - 0.5)[-seq_len(half), , drop = FALSE]     moon <- rbind(top, bot) * 6 + matrix(shift, per, 2, byrow = TRUE)     moon + matrix(rnorm(2 * per, sd = noise * 6), per)   }) |>     reduce(rbind)   if (d > 2) x <- cbind(x, matrix(rnorm(nrow(x) * (d - 2), sd = 0.05), nrow(x)))   x }  generators <- list(   gaussian_blobs = gen_gaussian_blobs,   anisotropic_blobs = gen_anisotropic_blobs,   uniform_cubes = gen_uniform_cubes,   moons_tiled = gen_moons_tiled )

code: race <- function(x, k, seed = 0) {   set.seed(seed)   init <- x[sample(nrow(x), k), ]   t_lloyd <- system.time(     km <- suppressWarnings(kmeans(x, init, iter.max = ITERS_LLOYD, algorithm = "Lloyd"))   )[["elapsed"]]   t_em <- system.time(     em <- emeans(x, init, nepochs = EPOCHS_EMEANS, seed = seed + 1)   )[["elapsed"]]   tibble(     lloyd_loss = km$tot.withinss / nrow(x),     emeans_loss = em$tot.withinss / nrow(x),     lloyd_s = t_lloyd,     emeans_s = t_em   ) }  run_races <- function(d) {   imap(generators, function(gen, name) {     set.seed(42)     x <- gen(N, K, d)  # generate before race() reseeds for its starting rows     race(x, K)   }) |>     list_rbind(names_to = "distribution") |>     mutate(emeans_vs_lloyd = sprintf("%+.1f%%", 100 * (emeans_loss / lloyd_loss - 1))) }  results <- run_races(D) knitr::kable(results, digits = 4) results |>   select(distribution, Lloyd = lloyd_loss, `e-means` = emeans_loss) |>   pivot_longer(-distribution, names_to = "method", values_to = "loss") |>   ggplot(aes(loss, distribution, fill = method)) +   geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6) +   scale_fill_manual(values = c(Lloyd = "#c0392b", `e-means` = "#2471a3")) +   labs(x = "final loss (mean squared distance)", y = NULL, fill = NULL,        title = "Lloyd at 25 passes vs. e-means at 8 passes") +   theme_minimal()

Packages: emeansR 0.1.0, Seurat 6.0.0. emeans() runs 7 threads. separate script ran slow steps (embedding, trees, reruns, stability, Louvain) saved every result disk. chunks show code, article reads saved results. code: system("gunzip -k .dev/data/GSE233163_seurat_object.rds.gz") full <- readRDS(".dev/data/GSE233163_seurat_object.rds") integrated <- full@assays$integrated obj <- CreateSeuratObject(CreateAssay5Object(data = integrated@data), assay = "integrated") VariableFeatures(obj) <- integrated@var.features rm(full, integrated) invisible(gc()) embedding <- local({   obj <- ScaleData(obj, verbose = FALSE)   obj <- RunPCA(obj, npcs = 30, seed.use = 12345, verbose = FALSE)   obj <- RunUMAP(obj, dims = 1:20, n.neighbors = 30, metric = "cosine", min.dist = 0.3,                  seed.use = 12345, verbose = FALSE)   list(pcs = Embeddings(obj, "pca")[, 1:20], umap = Embeddings(obj, "umap")) }) rm(obj) pcs <- embedding$pcs umap <- embedding$umap dim(pcs) #> [1] 73042    20  meta <- read.csv(".dev/data/GSE233163_cells_metadata.csv.gz") cell_type <- meta$cell_type[match(rownames(pcs), meta$id)] cell_group_map <- c(   endothelial_1 = "ECs", endothelial_2 = "ECs", endothelial_3 = "ECs",   pericyte = "Pericytes",   schwann_cell_1 = "Sc_NM", schwann_cell_2 = "Sc_NM",   schwann_cell_myelinating = "Sc_M",   neuron = "Neurons",   dendritic = "DCs",   microglia_1 = "Microglia",   macrophage = "Macrophages",   t_reg_lymphocyte = "Treg cells" ) cell_group_colours <- c(   ECs = "#22C41E", Pericytes = "#F5E50A", Sc_NM = "#1AA3E0", Sc_M = "#2B5FD9", Neurons = "#A3171D",   DCs = "#E3191C", Microglia = "#8E2A8E", Macrophages = "#000000", `Treg cells` = "#3CC9C0" ) cell_group <- factor(cell_group_map[cell_type], levels = names(cell_group_colours)) table(cell_group, useNA = "ifany") #> cell_group #>         ECs   Pericytes       Sc_NM        Sc_M     Neurons         DCs  #>        7731        1501       50080        3991         406        1707  #>   Microglia Macrophages  Treg cells  #>         470        5886        1270

title: A resolution tree for single-cell data
text: level tree refines one , resolutions nest: every cluster level 4 lies inside one cluster level 3. Louvain separate resolutions gives guarantee. split asks emeans() two clusters, nobody pick global number clusters advance. fits small (nepochs = 3), keeps whole tree cheap, every node gets seed, seed always gives tree. bisect_tree() keeps one label per cell depth. depth, emeans() splits every node least min_cells cells two, using node’s cells; smaller nodes keep label. label path root, "1.2.1" first child second child root.
code: bisect_tree <- function(x, max_depth = 5, min_cells = 200, seed = 1) {   labels <- matrix("1", nrow(x), max_depth + 1, dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("level_", 0:max_depth)))   for (depth in seq_len(max_depth)) {     parent <- labels[, depth]     child <- parent     nodes <- unique(parent)     for (i in seq_along(nodes)) {       idx <- which(parent == nodes[i])       if (length(idx) < min_cells) next       fit <- emeans(x[idx, , drop = FALSE], 2, nepochs = 3, seed = seed * 1000 + depth * 100 + i)       child[idx] <- paste0(nodes[i], ".", fit$cluster)     }     labels[, depth + 1] <- child   }   labels }  max_depth <- 5 tree_time <- system.time(tree <- bisect_tree(pcs, max_depth))[["elapsed"]] levels <- 1:max_depth n_clusters <- map_int(levels, ~ n_distinct(tree[, .x + 1])) tibble(level = levels, clusters = n_clusters) #> # A tibble: 5 × 2 #>   level clusters #>   <int>    <int> #> 1     1        2 #> 2     2        4 #> 3     3        8 #> 4     4       16 #> 5     5       31

code: reruns <- map(2:11, ~ bisect_tree(pcs, max_depth, seed = .x)) cell_jaccard <- function(a, b) {   tab <- table(a, b)   jac <- tab / (outer(rowSums(tab), colSums(tab), "+") - tab)   jac[cbind(match(a, rownames(tab)), match(b, colnames(tab)))] }  seed_ari <- map_dfr(seq_along(reruns), function(r) {   tibble(run = r, level = levels,          ari = map_dbl(levels, ~ adjustedRandIndex(tree[, .x + 1], reruns[[r]][, .x + 1]))) })  stability <- map(levels, function(l) {   rowMeans(sapply(reruns, function(run) cell_jaccard(tree[, l + 1], run[, l + 1]))) })

title: A resolution tree for single-cell data
text: Seurat’s FindClusters() runs range resolutions shared nearest neighbour graph 20 components (k.param = 20, authors used). tree level paired resolution whose cluster count closest . saved agreement table scores tree 12 metadata labels, chunk recomputes ARI 9 cell types. Louvain returns least 3 clusters even resolution 0.001, levels 1 2 compared coarsest Louvain partition.
code: resolutions <- c(0.001, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2) louvain_time <- system.time({   graphs <- FindNeighbors(pcs, k.param = 20, verbose = FALSE)   louvain <- FindClusters(graphs$snn, resolution = resolutions, verbose = FALSE) })[["elapsed"]] louvain_k <- map_int(louvain, n_distinct) match_res <- map_int(n_clusters, ~ which.min(abs(louvain_k - .x)))  agreement <- tibble(   level = levels,   clusters = n_clusters,   resolution = resolutions[match_res],   louvain_clusters = louvain_k[match_res],   ari_louvain = map2_dbl(levels, match_res, ~ adjustedRandIndex(tree[, .x + 1], louvain[[.y]])),   ari_cell_group = map_dbl(levels, ~ adjustedRandIndex(tree[, .x + 1], cell_group)) ) agreement <- read_result("agreement") |>   select(-ari_cell_type) |>   mutate(ari_cell_group = map_dbl(levels, ~ adjustedRandIndex(tree[, .x + 1], cell_group))) agreement #> # A tibble: 5 × 6 #>   level clusters resolution louvain_clusters ari_louvain ari_cell_group #>   <int>    <int>      <dbl>            <int>       <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1     1        2      0.001                3       0.163          0.187 #> 2     2        4      0.001                3       0.533          0.573 #> 3     3        8      0.01                 8       0.937          0.919 #> 4     4       16      0.2                 16       0.541          0.796 #> 5     5       31      1                   33       0.181          0.540

title: A resolution tree for single-cell data
text: Node size number cells; colour mean seed stability node’s cells depth. Leaf labels give common cell type among leaf’s cells.
code: node_stability <- map_dfr(levels, function(l) {   tibble(name = tree[, l + 1], stability = stability[[l]]) |>     group_by(name) |>     summarise(stability = mean(stability), .groups = "drop") |>     mutate(depth = l) })  # A node that stops splitting keeps its name at deeper levels; keep its first depth. nodes <- map_dfr(0:max_depth, ~ count(tibble(name = tree[, .x + 1]), name, name = "cells") |> mutate(depth = .x)) |>   group_by(name) |>   slice_min(depth) |>   ungroup() |>   left_join(node_stability, by = c("name", "depth"))  edges <- nodes |>   filter(depth > 0) |>   transmute(from = sub("\\.[^.]+$", "", name), to = name)  # The last tree column holds each cell's leaf, also for nodes that stopped splitting early. leaf_group <- tibble(name = tree[, max_depth + 1], cell_group = cell_group) |>   count(name, cell_group) |>   group_by(name) |>   slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>   ungroup() |>   transmute(name, cell_group = as.character(cell_group),             label_colour = cell_group_colours[cell_group])  graph <- tbl_graph(nodes = left_join(nodes, leaf_group, by = "name"), edges = edges) |>   mutate(leaf = node_is_leaf()) ggraph(graph, layout = "dendrogram", height = -depth) +   geom_edge_elbow(colour = "grey60") +   geom_node_point(aes(size = cells, colour = stability)) +   geom_node_text(aes(label = cell_group, colour = I(label_colour), filter = leaf),                  angle = 90, hjust = 1, nudge_y = -0.2, size = 2.8, fontface = "bold") +   scale_colour_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "grey40") +   scale_size_area(max_size = 8) +   expand_limits(y = -max_depth - 1.3) +   labs(colour = "seed\nstability", size = "cells") +   theme_void()

Louvain needs shared nearest neighbour graph first, built , runs resolution one job. e-means gets one job per cluster count Louvain produced. forked worker takes one job one core, script repeats every step three times reports medians. Tree levels depend , tree runs sequence gives emeans() cores threads. 7 cores, Seurat sweep (graph plus 14 resolutions) takes 84.5 seconds, 10.7 building graph. e-means 14 cluster counts takes 1.1 seconds, whole five-level tree 0.2 seconds.

text: R implementation e-means (Bessa et al., 2026, arXiv:2611.09501), mini-batch replacement Lloyd’s k-means. centroid follows exponential moving average mini-batch means, fitted scaling laws set batch size step size, supply data, k epoch budget. paper reports lower within-cluster sum squares 25 Lloyd iterations epochs; benchmark shows holds. compute core (nearest-centroid assignment EMA updates) Rust, multi-threaded CPU. training recipe follows reference library, faiss/contrib/e_means, gives batch size step size n, k, d epoch budget.

title: e-means clustering — emeans
text: Mini-batch k-means exponential-moving-average centroid updates (Bessa et al., 2026, arXiv:2611.09501). Batch size step size come fitted scaling laws, inputs data, k, epoch budget. epochs typically reaches lower within-cluster sum squares 25 Lloyd iterations.

title: e-means clustering — emeans

title: e-means clustering — emeans
text: x Numeric matrix data frame, one row per point. k Number clusters, k x d matrix initial centers. nepochs Epoch budget; fractions allowed (e.g. 1.5). batch_law "auto" (quality law d <= 16, else throughput), "throughput", "quality" (batch 8 times smaller). batch_size, alpha0 Optional overrides. Giving batch_size alone keeps step law alpha0. spherical Cluster unit vectors cosine similarity. Rows x must already unit-norm; centers returned unit vectors. unused_threshold Revival threshold tau: clusters mass tau * mean(mass) revived. NULL gives 0.1, 0 () d <= 2. max_points_per_centroid set nrow(x) > max_points_per_centroid * k, train random subset many rows (faiss.Kmeans). precision "double", "single" store training data compute distances float32 (2x faster, half memory). Batch statistics, centroids masses always accumulate double precision, withinss computed original data. faiss FP32 path, single precision assigns poorly data sit far origin (error grows squared norm rows); centre data first, e.g. scale(x, scale = FALSE). Double precision hits limit offsets around 1e8. final_assign TRUE (default), assign every row x final centers, cluster, withinss size describe returned centers (stats::kmeans()). FALSE, cluster holds labels last training pass, rows left max_points_per_centroid NA. seed Integer seed initialization, shuffling revival. touch R's random number generator. n_threads Threads assignment. Defaults getOption("emeansR.threads"), else physical cores minus one (two _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_ environment variable set). verbose Print recipe per-epoch objective.

title: e-means clustering — emeans
text: object class c("emeans", "kmeans") components cluster, centers, totss, withinss, tot.withinss, betweenss, size, iter (epochs), ifault (0), plus obj (moving-pass objective per epoch), iteration_stats, recipe, n_splits, spherical precision.

title: e-means clustering — emeans
text: epoch visits rows fresh random order batches batch_size. Every batch assigned nearest centroids, touched centroid moves towards batch mean weight alpha * n_j / N_j, mass N_j exponential moving average alpha follows cosine schedule alpha0 alpha0 / 10. Every five updates, clusters mass unused_threshold * mean(mass) revived splitting large clusters (picked probability proportional mass). returned centers exact means points assigned last epoch.

code: s <- emeans_stream(n, init, nepochs = 3) for (epoch in seq_along(s$recipe$epoch_rows)) {   left <- s$recipe$epoch_rows[epoch]   while (left > 0) {     b <- emeans_stream_status(s)$expected_batch     emeans_accumulate(s, next_rows(b))  # next_rows(): your data reader     emeans_update(s)     left <- left - b   }   emeans_end_epoch(s) } fit <- emeans_finalize(s)

title: emeansR 0.1.0
text: First release. emeans() fits e-means (Bessa et al., 2026, arXiv:2611.09501): mini-batch k-means exponential moving average centroid updates. batch size initial step come scaling laws reference library, faiss/contrib/e_means, match exactly data size, number clusters, dimension epoch budget. result also inherits kmeans, cluster, centers, size, withinss tot.withinss work usual. predict() labels new rows. emeans_stream() companions train data supplied chunks, data fit memory. spherical = TRUE clusters unit vectors cosine similarity; precision = "single" computes distances single precision; max_points_per_centroid trains random subset. emeans_recipe() shows batch size step scaling laws choose. compute core written Rust runs several threads. Rust dependencies bundled, installation needs network access. Needs rustc 1.71 later. pkgdown site two articles: port authors’ CPU demo, benchmark kmeans(), hclust() Mclust().
